task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of September 8, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about temporary repair businesses occupying part of Ambercourt mall's vacant former department store and the opportunities and limits of a short lease.

facts.text: An August 2026 site note describes upholsterer Rena Selt showing a customer two replacement chair fabrics in a unit formerly used to display luggage.
Ambercourt mall has divided part of its vacant department-store space into eight temporary workshop-retail units.
Five units were occupied at the end of July and three remained available.
A unit's weekly charge is $150 rent plus $35 for shared utilities, totaling $185 a week before the tenant's other expenses.
The agreements renew in 28-day periods for up to six months and provide 14 days' notice if the landlord ends the arrangement.
The landlord is still seeking a long-term tenant for the former anchor space and has not promised permanent workshops.
Selt uses the unit for customer meetings, fabric cutting and small repairs, while dusty stripping work remains at a separate workspace.
The mall's temporary-use rules exclude large saws and spray finishing inside these units.
Selt completed eight paid repair jobs in her first month and made three additional quick adjustments without a charge.
Those job counts do not establish profit after rent, materials, labor and the cost of the separate workspace.
Selt said, "A shop window lets people bring a question in. A four-week lease makes me careful about what I leave behind."
Customer Oren Bell says seeing fabric samples in person helped him decide whether to repair chairs rather than replace them.
Bell asked how to contact Selt if the mall unit closes before a later repair is needed.
Selt's written work orders list her business contact details separately from the temporary unit address.
Mall manager Ceri Marel says the arrangement generates some rent and occupied frontage while negotiations with prospective anchor tenants continue.
Marel said, "We can offer a beginning here without pretending we have already found a permanent ending for the building."
The mall counted 320 visits to the workshop area during one observed week but has no comparable count for the former department store.
The visit count is not a count of repair purchases or evidence that the entire mall has recovered commercially.
The original department store closed in 2024, leaving some display rails and old fitting-room mirrors in place.
No permanent anchor lease, tenant profit survey or mall-wide employment recovery has been announced.

forbidden_additions: Permanent workshops, proven tenant profits or complete mall recovery
All observed visits resulted in paid repairs or every repair process can occur in the unit
